rules.title: Residential rental application fee capped at $50
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge more than $50 as an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental. Violators face penalties of up to $500 (first), $750 (second) and $1,000 (each later offense), and the overcharge is refunded to the applicant.
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador o su agente no puede cobrar más de $50 por una solicitud o tarifa similar para alquilar o subarrendar una vivienda residencial. Las infracciones conllevan multas de hasta $500 (primera), $750 (segunda) y $1,000 (cada una posterior), y el cobro excesivo se devuelve al solicitante.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental properties statewide, except one- and two-family dwellings offered for rent and New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensees (unless the licensee is the landlord).
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in a one-family or two-family dwelling; licensees of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission unless the licensee is the landlord.
rules.penalty: Up to $500 first offense, up to $750 second offense, up to $1,000 each subsequent offense; amount wrongfully charged remitted to applicant.
rules.effective_date_quote: This act shall take effect on the first day of the fourth month next following the date of enactment
rules.caveat: The $50 limit is adjusted each January 1 by CPI change (only if positive), so the current cap may exceed $50. Effective date computed from approval on January 20, 2026.
